### Observed differences

- In the later window, each of the eight activities A28, A29, A31, A32, A33, A34, A35 and A36 runs in essentially every case (199 of 200 traces each), whereas earlier each ran in only about half of the cases — about 54 in 100 for A28/A29/A31/A32 and about 46 in 100 for A33–A36. In both windows each of them occurs at most once per case. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008]
- Earlier, the two groups of four were mutually exclusive: cross-group pairs such as A28–A33 or A31–A36 co-occurred in 0 of 200 cases, each case containing one group or the other. In the later window, every cross-group pair co-occurs in about 99 in 100 cases, always with the A28/A29/A31/A32 activity before the A33–A36 activity. [REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL026, REL027, REL028, REL029, REL031, REL032, REL033, REL034, REL035, REL036, REL037, REL038]
- A25 now comes before all eight activities in 199 of 200 cases, where earlier it came before whichever group was present (about 54 and 46 in 100 respectively) and never before the absent group; A26 now comes after all eight in 199 of 200 cases, where earlier it came after the single present group. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016]
- Order within each group of four remains unordered: within-group pairs co-occur in nearly all later cases (earlier in about half, with the pair absent otherwise), but their relative order stays close to 50/50. [REL017, REL018, REL019, REL024, REL025, REL030, REL039, REL040, REL041, REL042, REL043, REL044]
- Routing changed accordingly: from A25, outgoing transitions earlier spread over all eight group activities (about 9–15% each), while in the later window they go almost exclusively to A28/A29/A31/A32 (about 20–29% each). From each of A28, A29, A31 and A32, the transition to A26 (about 22–29% of outgoing transitions earlier) is no longer observed, and new transitions to A33–A36 (about 4–8% each) appear. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
- Positions and spacings shift as expected for a longer middle segment: A25's mean relative position moves earlier (0.66 to 0.58), A28–A32 move earlier (about 0.74 to about 0.65) and A33–A36 slightly later (about 0.74 to about 0.77); the measured distance from A25 to A33–A36 and from A28–A32 to A26, spread over 1–4 steps earlier, sits at 5 steps in about 98 of 100 later cases where the pair falls within five steps (43–56 cases each). [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008, POS009, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the segment between A25 and A26 changed from running one of two alternative groups of four activities to running both groups in sequence: in the later window, cases appear to execute A28, A29, A31 and A32 in varying order, then A33, A34, A35 and A36 in varying order, between A25 at the start and A26 at the end. The support is direct and consistent: cross-group pairs that never co-occurred earlier (0 of 200 cases) co-occur in about 99 in 100 later cases with the first group always ahead, participation of all eight activities rose from about half of cases to essentially all, the routing into and out of the segment changed in line with this, and the distance-5 measurements match a fixed four-activity block between the anchors. With 74 flagged items against roughly 0.78 expected by chance across the 157 tested units, and every difference larger than in about 995 of 1000 random re-splits, chance alone cannot explain the pattern as a whole. [REL020, REL026, REL031, REL035, OCC001, OCC005, DIR001, DIR002, LAG001, LAG005]

Limitations remain: the many relation items largely restate one underlying flip and are not independent confirmations. The evidence also cannot rule out that both behaviours already existed and only their frequencies shifted — a case containing both groups appeared 0 times in 200 earlier traces, so such cases could have existed at up to roughly 1–2 in 100 cases before, and a wholesale shift in the mix of pre-existing variants would look identical here. Unobserved transitions (such as A28 to A26 in the later window) do not prove those edges are gone, and the lag items rest on only 43–56 later cases each. [REL020, DIR002, LAG001]
